content: 1. Pegloticase may reduce the levels or effects of peginterferon alfa-2b due to the potential development of anti-PEG antibodies that could bind to other PEGylated drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 2. Most patients treated with pegvaliase develop anti-polyethylene glycol (PEG) IgM and IgG antibodies. The risk of coadministration with other PEGylated products is unknown. There is a reported case of anaphylaxis following the use of a medroxyprogesterone acetate injectable suspension containing PEG 3350. Carefully review all drug labels, including over-the-counter medications, for PEG content. 3. When peginterferon alfa-2b is coadministered with CYP2D6 substrates, the therapeutic effects of these drugs may be altered. Peginterferon alfa-2b can either increase or decrease the levels of CYP2D6 substrates. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 4. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases phenytoin levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 5. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases tamoxifen levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 6. Peginterferon alfa-2b increases the levels of theophylline through an unknown mechanism. Alpha interferons may reduce the clearance of theophylline, leading to increased plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 7. Peginterferon alfa-2b increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 8. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases voriconazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 9. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases zafirlukast levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 10. Peginterferon alfa-2b increases the levels or effects of zidovudine. Interferons may enhance the adverse effects of zidovudine, including increased myelosuppression. Monitor patients closely. 11. Coadministration of peginterferon alfa-2b with acalabrutinib may increase the risk of myelosuppressive effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 12. Peginterferon alfa-2b increases the toxicity of aldesleukin through an unknown mechanism. Interferons may enhance the adverse effects of aldesleukin, including myocardial and renal toxicity. Monitor patients closely. 13. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases bosentan levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 14. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 15. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 16. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 17. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 18. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 19. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 20. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases glipizide levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 21. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases levels of torsemide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. The therapeutic effects of CYP2C9 substrates may be altered when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b. 22. Peginterferon alfa-2b is contraindicated with fezolinetant due to its effect on hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism, leading to increased fezolinetant AUC and peak plasma concentrations. Avoid coadministration. 23. Peginterferon alfa-2b may alter the therapeutic effects of CYP2D6 substrates, such as amitriptyline, aripiprazole, atomoxetine, clomipramine, codeine, desipramine, dextromethorphan, duloxetine, fluoxetine, flecainide, fluvoxamine, risperidone, sertraline, tramadol, trazodone, trimipramine, and venlafaxine. It may increase or decrease the levels of these drugs. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 24. Peginterferon alfa-2b increases the toxicity of deferiprone due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If no alternative is available, monitor the absolute neutrophil count more frequently. 25. Peginterferon alfa-2b increases the levels or effects of zidovudine, potentially enhancing adverse effects such as myelosuppression. Monitor patients closely.
